- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged rally; cap forecast peak at 2–3 days above true peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope sharply after sentiment drop.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 7 days if sentiment is mixed or bearish.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is flat, model tends to overpredict volatility; forecast should be within ±1% of recent 7-day average.
